summary.rationale: All four items consume canonical_constants.py as input data but none update/extend the knowledge-MCP schema, add new canonical constants, run /weave --update, or query the knowledge-index. They are physics computations (cohomology cocycle, Petrov classification grid densification, Pontryagin on non-flat base, K-corridor L_max stability) that happen to live in the knowledge-mcp theme bucket only because canonical_constants is listed in their inputs. Under conservative merge, reading canonical_constants as input is not the same shared-infrastructure action and does not justify a merge.
